fields.meta_description: Build a course evaluation survey with module ratings, phone answers, low-score alerts, and results by client, saved to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Course Evaluation Survey for Every Course You Teach
fields.hero_description: Build a course evaluation survey that rates each module, flags low scores, and saves every answer to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Course Evaluation Survey on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Describe the course and who reads the results. Emergent builds each piece below, and a follow-up prompt changes any of them.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each part of the course

Name the modules, sessions, or lessons your course runs. Emergent drafts a rating question and a comment question for each part, and one more sentence rewords any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer tagged by course and cohort

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the course, cohort, and date on it. Set this cohort's module scores beside the last one before you plan the next run.
fields.feature_3:
An email when a rating falls to 1 or 2

A rating of 1 or 2 sends the instructor an email with the student's comment beside it, while the lesson is fresh. Slack alerts work too, and reminders reach anyone yet to answer.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Students scan the code on your last slide and answer one question per screen on a phone, before they pack up. No response cap applies, whether 12 students answer or 1,200 do.
fields.feature_5:
Linked to your course platform

Connect the survey to your course platform or any tool with an API. The app can send the link when a student finishes the last lesson and sync each answer to that student's record.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain and your code

Publish the survey on your own domain: custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository for a developer to extend.

fields.tab_content_1:
The frameworks module ran too fast for 17 of 26 students

Quenby Code School asks each bootcamp cohort to rate every module on a 1-5 scale on the last day. Of 28 spring students, 26 answered. HTML and CSS averaged 4.5, JavaScript 4.2, and databases 4.1. Frameworks scored 3.1, and 17 of the 26 called its pace too fast. The next cohort gets 2 weeks on it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Glazing wins 8 of 14 votes and a second night

On the last night of its 6-week wheel course, Thistlecombe Clay Studio tapes a QR code by the kilns. The survey opens on each phone, one question per screen. Of 16 students, 14 said which session needs more time: 8 picked glazing, 4 trimming, and 2 centering. The next course adds a second glazing night.
fields.tab_content_3:
Lesson 7 is re-recorded after it draws 4 of 5 low ratings

Ondine Pryor's self-paced bookkeeping course opens the evaluation once a student completes the final lesson. Of 64 August finishers, 41 answered. Any rating of 1 or 2 emails Ondine with the comment. August brought 5, and 4 named lesson 7 on bank reconciliations. She re-recorded it around a slower worked example.
fields.tab_content_4:
One of 4 clients scores the case studies 2.8

Larkhaven Training runs a 2-day project management course for client companies and tags answers by client. Across 4 clients, 67 trainees answered. Three rated the case studies 4.1 to 4.4. Ivybridge Medical Group rated them 2.8 and asked for hospital examples. Larkhaven wrote 2 before Ivybridge's next cohort.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Course Evaluation Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a course evaluation survey, build it with Emergent, and turn the lowest score into a change for the next run.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick what the results could change
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add two open questions at the end
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the answers could change before the next run, such as a module to lengthen or a lesson to re-record. Write that in the first line of your prompt to Emergent. Cut any question whose answer could not move that decision.
fields.howto_step_2_des: List each module or session, then add the materials, the pace, and the workload. Rate every one on the same 1-5 scale, so a weak part stands out against the rest and against the previous cohort's scores.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent the course name, its parts, who answers, and who reads the results. Emergent builds the survey and a results dashboard from that description. Ask for any change in one more sentence, such as a new module or a reworded question.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Close with two optional questions: what should stay exactly as it is, and what should change next time. A rating tells you where a course is weak. The comments tell you what to do about it, in the students' own words.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Test it with two past students
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the link to 2 people who took the course before and ask them to answer on a phone. Watch for a question they read two ways or a module name they do not recognize, and fix it before launch.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Open it before the last session ends
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run the survey during the final session instead of emailing it a week later. UW-Madison's assessment office suggests giving students 10-15 minutes of class time to complete it. Send one reminder to anyone still out after that.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Tell the next cohort what changed
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the survey closes, compare each part's score with the last run and pick one change to make. On day one of the next run, tell students what earlier students asked for and what you changed because of it.

faq_plan.q: What is a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.ref: What is a course evaluation survey?

prov.original: What is a course evaluation survey?

faq_plan.a: A course evaluation survey asks the people who took a course to rate its parts and say what should change. It covers modules or sessions, materials, pace, and workload, plus a few open comments. The answers tell the instructor or training provider what is working and what to fix before the course runs again.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.a: Write a plain-English prompt that names the course and the parts students will rate. Emergent's AI survey builder builds the survey from it, with a database for the answers and a dashboard for the scores. Publish the link, and edit any question later with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to ask in a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to ask in a course evaluation survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to ask in a course evaluation survey?

faq_plan.a: Ask students to rate each module or session from 1 to 5, then rate the pace and how well the assessments matched what was taught. Add whether they would recommend the course, and two open questions on what to keep and what to change. Good course evaluation survey questions name the part being rated. Then every low score points at something you can fix.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse one course evaluation survey template for every course I teach?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the core. Keep the same rating questions and scale in every course. Scores then compare across courses and cohorts. Swap in each course's own module names, and add a question or two for its format. If an association runs your courses for its members, keep the evaluation apart from its yearly membership survey.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a course evaluation survey have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 10 to 15 questions, short enough to finish before students leave the room. Give one rating to each module and one each to pace and materials, then close with two open questions. A long course can stay short too: rate its modules in groups instead of one by one.

faq_plan.q: What is the best time to run a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.a: Run the end-of-course ratings in the final session. For a course longer than 6 weeks, also add a 3-question check at the midpoint, while the pace can still change for the same group. A self-paced course can send it as each student reaches the end.

faq_plan.q: Does a course evaluation survey work for a live online class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Keep the same module and pace ratings, and add one question on whether the audio and shared screens worked. For a single one-hour online session rather than a full course, a short post webinar survey fits better. Emergent puts no response cap on either one.

faq_plan.q: Should course evaluation surveys be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Yes. UW-Madison's assessment office notes that students are hesitant to complete course evaluations if they feel they may be identified by their responses. Leave out demographic questions in a small class, where they could point to one student, and say in the invitation who reads the raw comments.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best in a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.a: A 5-point scale, used the same way on every question. Label both ends, such as 1 for poor and 5 for excellent, and keep the higher number meaning better throughout. Averages then compare across modules. Add a not-applicable choice for a part a student missed. Every answer lands in a database you own, and this term's scores sit beside last term's.

faq_plan.q: Should a one-day workshop get a course evaluation survey?
faq_plan.a: Yes, a short one. Rate each part of the day and whether the pace fit, then ask one open question. If the day was a conference or a networking event with no curriculum to rate, a post event survey is the better choice. Emergent builds either one from a plain-English prompt.

plan.angle: Seven of the top 10 are universities' own course evaluation systems and question banks, written for their own faculty, and the two tool slots are a template page and an institutional platform. This page is for instructors and training providers outside a university: a coding bootcamp, a clay studio, a solo online instructor, and a corporate training firm. Each tab ends in a change to the course itself (a module split, an extra class night, a re-recorded lesson, new case studies), not a rating of the instructor, which the teacher evaluation page covers. The FAQ answers the question searches (what to ask, template reuse, length, timing, anonymity, response rates) as plain advice, two points sourced to UW-Madison's guidance.
